title: Messi Calls World Cup Final 'The Last Tango' in Emotional Farewell Before Argentina Face Spain
excerpt: The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner posted a tribute to his teammates and unveiled boots named 'The Last Tango' ahead of Sunday's final in New Jersey, strongly hinting this will be his last World Cup match.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Messi's Instagram post hints at retirement, calling the final 'The Last Tango' with over 10 million likes.
  • Argentina faces Spain in the World Cup final, with Messi aiming for back-to-back titles at age 39.
  • Messi shared an emotional team photo, emphasizing the unforgettable journey with his teammates.
  • Spain has only conceded one goal in the tournament, seeking their second World Cup title since 2010.
Messi's Emotional Farewell
›Instagram post received over 10 million likes.
›Messi's boots named 'The Last Tango'.
›Messi's age: 39 years old.
›Final match against Spain on Sunday.
  • Lionel Messi called the World Cup final against Spain "The Last Tango" in an Instagram post that received more than 10 million likes, strongly hinting at international retirement.
  • Argentina face Spain at New York New Jersey Stadium on Sunday at 3 p.m. ET, with Messi, 39, bidding for back-to-back World Cups.
  • In an emotional team photo, Messi wrote: "Whatever happens tomorrow, this group has already written a story we'll never forget and that no one can erase."
  • Spain have conceded just one goal in the entire tournament and are chasing their second World Cup title after 2010.

Lionel Messi delivered what read unmistakably like a farewell on the eve of the World Cup final, calling Sunday's match against Spain "The Last Tango" and posting an emotional tribute to his Argentina teammates that all but confirmed this will be his final appearance on football's biggest stage.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner, 39, shared two posts on Instagram ahead of the final at New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford. The first featured Messi draped in an Argentina flag alongside a photo of his blue-and-white adidas boots — named "The Last Tango" — and the caption: "What a journey we're having together, @adidasfootball… with 'The Last Tango'… Let's go for the final, let's go Argentina!!!"

https://x.com/JefferyCrypt/status/2078435933402149272

The post surpassed 10 million likes within hours.

""Whatever happens tomorrow, this group has already written a story we'll never forget and that no one can erase."

A Letter to the Team

The second post was more personal. Messi shared a large team photo including every player and staff member, accompanied by a message that read like a captain's final letter.

"The best part of all these years wasn't just the titles, but the whole journey. Sharing every day with this group, competing together, getting back up in tough times, and enjoying every step."

— Lionel Messi

"Thank you to each of my teammates, the coaching staff, and everyone who works every day to keep this national team a family," Messi wrote. "Whatever happens tomorrow, this group has already written a story we'll never forget and that no one can erase. GO ARGENTINA."

At 39, Messi is almost certainly too old to compete at the 2030 World Cup, which will be co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco. He remains under contract with Inter Miami through December 2028 after signing a three-year extension last October, and scored 12 goals in 14 MLS appearances this season before the World Cup.

Argentina vs. Spain Showdown
›Argentina's semifinal victory: 2-1 against England.
›Spain conceded only 1 goal in 6 matches.
›Lamine Yamal, 19, faces his idol Messi.
›FIFA's winner's prize: $50 million.

The Final: Argentina vs. Spain

Argentina's path to the final included a 2-1 semifinal victory over England, with both goals coming in the second half. Spain, meanwhile, have been the tournament's most dominant team, conceding just a single goal across six matches. Former Ballon d'Or winner Rodri has called Argentina "the toughest rival," while Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente described both squads as "super teams."

The matchup brings together football's present and future. Spain's 19-year-old Lamine Yamal — the teenager famously photographed as a baby with Messi in 2007 — will line up against his childhood idol. Messi addressed the connection with characteristic grace at a press event on Friday: "He is one of the best players in the world right now. He's only 19 years old and he has all of his future ahead. That picture… it was crazy. Him as a baby, and now we are facing each other."

He smiled before adding: "What's good for him will also be good for Barcelona."

Stakes for Indian Fans

The World Cup final has captivated Indian football fans, with Messi commanding a massive following across the subcontinent. Argentina and Brazil have historically been the two most supported teams among Indian fans, and Messi's potential farewell adds emotional weight to a match already loaded with sporting significance. The final kicks off at 12:30 a.m. IST on Monday, a time slot that has not stopped millions of Indian viewers from tuning in throughout the tournament.

The match will be broadcast on FOX in the United States and is available on streaming platforms including Peacock and Fubo TV. FIFA's record $50 million winner's prize and a halftime show featuring Madonna, Shakira and BTS add to the spectacle surrounding what could be the last act of football's greatest career.
